answer: A single ember checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 291 aliases therefore costs 201 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the terrace attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a falcon, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
